components.css: .ds-tiles{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:8px}.ds-tile{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;min-height:62px;padding:8px 12px 8px 8px;border-radius:var(--r3,22px);background:var(--s2);color:var(--bright);border:0;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;font:14px Figtree,system-ui,sans-serif;transition:background 220ms cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1),border-radius 360ms cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1),scale 120ms}.ds-tile:active{scale:.96}.ds-tile:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:2px}.ds-tile .ic{width:42px;height:42px;border-radius:var(--r2,16px);display:grid;place-items:center;background:var(--s3);transition:border-radius 360ms cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)}.ds-tile b{display:block;font-weight:600;font-size:13px}.ds-tile small{display:block;font-size:11px;color:var(--dim)}.ds-tile.on{background:var(--accent);color:var(--on-accent);border-radius:calc(var(--r3,22px) + 8px)}.ds-tile.on small{color:var(--on-accent)}.ds-tile.on .ic{background:color-mix(in oklab,var(--on-accent),transparent 84%);border-radius:50%}

Software encoding

This computer has no working video encoder, so the picture uses more CPU and may lag.

narrative.overview:
wado's chrome is the shell around someone else's screen. It works in two phases, and the second
is the one already built. **Glass Cockpit** (incumbent): the streamed desktop owns the whole
display and every control floats over it as an instrument: a thumb-reachable dock that fades when
idle, a link badge in the corner, a control centre that slides up as a sheet. Nothing reflows the
picture. **Pocket Console** (decided `2026-10-29`, not yet built): by default, a session opens
with the screen drawn smaller at its true aspect ratio, held inside a console-like shell whose
controls sit *around* it. Going full screen grows the picture to take the whole display, and the
same controls morph outward into the floating cockpit instruments. They are one set of controls
in two arrangements, never two UIs. The candidates for the console's surround are window controls
(resize, close, minimise, switching), input controls (touchpad, keys, gamepad, playback), and
status with quick tiles. The final arrangement is undecided.

The mood is **calm, tactile, honest**. Surfaces are soft, filled and pressable, moving on a spring
with a little mass. The chrome stays quiet until something is wrong, then says so in plain words
and the theme's own warning colours. Personality comes from the user's chosen base16 scheme and
from motion. Decoration is not where it lives.
keyCharacteristics: Every colour comes from sixteen swappable base16 slots; derived tokens are mixes, never hex.
The stage behind the video is always black, whatever the theme.
Tonal elevation (a mixed surface ladder) plus soft shadows only on floating chrome.
Two motion curves for the whole UI: a massy spring and a small overshoot pop.
The user tunes corner radius, motion level and accent slot from the Appearance page.

rules.name: The Sixteen Slots Rule
rules.body: No stylesheet hard-codes a colour. Every value is a base16 slot or a `color-mix` of slots. The only exceptions are Stage Black and black shadow/scrim mixes.

rules.name: The Mixed Ladder Rule
rules.body: Elevation is mixed from base00 toward base05, never read from base01 or base02. Schemes disagree about whether base01 is lighter or darker than base00, and only the mix gives a correct ladder on every scheme, light ones included.

rules.name: The Untouchable Picture Rule
rules.body: The theme may never change how the stream reads. A light ground bleeds onto the picture, so the stage stays black.

rules.name: The Sixteen-Pixel Input Rule
rules.body: Every text input is exactly 16px. Below that, iOS Safari zooms on focus and the streamed picture jumps sideways.

rules.name: The Machine Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: A value the system generated (an address, a resolution, a count) is set in mono. Words a person reads are set in Figtree.

rules.name: The Picture Owns The Screen Rule
rules.body: In the cockpit phase no chrome takes layout space from the video. Chrome floats over it and only dims what is behind. The Pocket Console phase relaxes this deliberately: the picture is inset at its true aspect ratio until the user goes full screen.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is floating over the picture". Content inside a sheet or card stays flat and gets its depth from tone.

rules.name: The Morphing Toggle Rule
rules.body: A control that turns on changes shape as well as colour. A tile's radius grows by 8px and its icon well becomes a circle. A switch's thumb grows from 16 to 24px.

dos: Do take every colour from a base16 slot or a `color-mix` of slots; add new roles as mixes in `base.css`.
Do keep the stage behind the video `#000`, whatever the scheme.
Do move things only with `transform`/`opacity` or the independent `translate`/`scale` properties, so the motion stays off the main thread and away from video decode.

Do use `--spring` (cubic-bezier(.32, .72, 0, 1)) for sheets and pages, and `--pop` (cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1)) for small things a finger just flipped. Use `--dur` (220ms) and `--dur-sheet` (480ms).
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion` and the user's `data-motion` (full / reduced / off).
Do keep touch targets at 44px or more, and text inputs at exactly 16px.
Do state a degraded link or encoder in plain words with its tone colour, and keep the technical name one tap away.
Do make the cockpit and console arrangements of a control the same control, morphing between them.
donts: Don't hard-code hex or `rgb()` in chrome. `files.css` currently does (`#888`, `#eee`, `#fff`, `rgb(20 20 22 / .94)` in the viewer). That is drift, and it should be brought back to tokens.
Don't read elevation from base01 or base02. Mix it.
Don't let chrome reflow the picture in the cockpit phase, or put a banner across it. Health lives in the dock LED, a toast or a hero chip.
Don't put shadows on content inside a sheet or card.
Don't enable backdrop blur on coarse-pointer devices.
Don't introduce a third easing curve, or a fourth font family.
Don't show a control that does nothing yet. A feature lands its tile when it lands.
